h1: Nakamanda Resort & Spa — teak villas on the beach at the quietest corner of Klong Muang
intro: If The Tubkaak sits right at the end of the coast, Klong Muang Beach is the quiet stretch just before it — far enough from the bustle of Ao Nang yet still easy to reach. Right on this beach sits Nakamanda Resort & Spa, a 5-star boutique resort that chooses teak, stone and contemporary Thai design over glass-tower glamour. Its 39 villas, many with a private plunge pool or jacuzzi, are spread through leafy gardens that open onto the Andaman Sea. From approx. THB 6,000/night.

body.html: Nakamanda is a small boutique resort of just 39 villas on Klong Muang Beach, Nong Thale. The thing every review agrees on is the design — teak, stone and warm contemporary-Thai tones that make it feel calmer and more characterful than the average new-build resort. The villas are scattered through tropical gardens, many opening straight onto the Andaman Sea, with Krabi's signature limestone karsts as a backdrop.

Rooms start with the Sala Villa at around 56 sqm, which feels generously sized, with a day bed, a private balcony or terrace, and a large bathroom that has a plunge tub separate from the shower. Step up and you reach the Hydropool and Jacuzzi Villa Seaview categories with a private hydro/jacuzzi tub, up to a two-bedroom Pool Villa Seaview for families. Guests love the privacy of the villas, but a common note is that the resort has a lot of steps and ramps across its hillside setting — anyone who can't manage stairs easily should request a lower villa in advance.
"Waking up to soak in the plunge pool outside the villa, looking out at the sea and the karst cliffs, so quiet you only hear the waves — it felt like having a beach of your own."

Dining centres on the beachfront Naga Terrace, serving Thai and international dishes. Breakfast earns praise for its live cooking station for eggs and made-to-order drinks, plus healthy options. The point several reviews make honestly is that the lunch and dinner menu isn't hugely varied and restaurant service can be slow — something you do see at small resorts that sit a fair way from town restaurants.

Beyond the beach and food, there's the Naga Spa, praised for good treatments and a relaxing setting, plus free kayaks and yoga classes, an outdoor pool and a fitness room. What reviews single out as the real strength is the warm staff who remember guests' names — being a small resort makes the service feel personal and attentive in a way the big chains nearby often don't match.

To be straight with you, the trade-off is the location, about 20 minutes from Ao Nang and roughly 30–40 minutes from Krabi airport. If you want to head out to eat, hit a bar or catch an island boat every day, that distance starts to bite, and Klong Muang itself has almost nothing happening after dark beyond the resort. Some reviews also feel the rates run a little high compared with similar-tier resorts in Thailand, especially in high season.

With a 9.0 from 65 Trip.com reviews (and around #8 of 18 Krabi hotels on TripAdvisor), Nakamanda suits couples and anyone after a quiet, design-led beach villa rather than a central base. The tip: if budget allows, choose a sea-view or Jacuzzi villa, because the Andaman views and karst cliffs are the main reason people come. On a tighter budget, the garden-view Sala Villa still gets you the same quiet beach — you just walk out to the water yourself.

honestSummary: Nakamanda is a strong pick for travellers who want a design-led villa on a quiet beach with personal service rather than a central location. The teak craftsmanship, Andaman views and sense of privacy are what guests remember — but accept the trade-offs: it's far from Ao Nang, there are lots of steps, and rates run on the high side.
honestChecks: If you want to walk out to restaurants, bars or island boats easily — Klong Muang is about 20 minutes from Ao Nang and dead quiet at night → a hotel in the Ao Nang area will be far more convenient.
If you or anyone in your group struggles with stairs — the resort has many steps and ramps across its hillside → request a lower villa near the pool/restaurant in advance.
If you want a direct sea view from your villa — the Sala Villa garden category looks onto gardens, not the sea → choose a Seaview or Jacuzzi Villa Seaview and book early in high season.

tips.title: Pick a sea-view villa if budget allows
tips.body: The Andaman views and karst cliffs are the main reason to come. The garden-view Sala Villa is cheaper, but for the sea upgrade to a Sea View or Jacuzzi Villa Seaview.

tips.title: Request a lower villa if stairs are tough
tips.body: The resort sits on a hillside with plenty of steps and ramps. If you have older travellers or limited mobility, ask the front desk for a villa near the pool/restaurant in advance.

tips.title: Use the free kayaks and yoga
tips.body: Kayaks and yoga classes are complimentary. An early-morning paddle along Klong Muang Beach when the water is calm is when the sea looks its best.

tips.title: Rent a car or arrange transfers
tips.body: It's a way from town and Ao Nang. If you plan to eat out or do island trips, renting a car or pre-booking transfers works out better than ordering Grab every time.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Nakamanda Resort & Spa, Krabi

faq.q: Where is Nakamanda Resort and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's on Klong Muang Beach, Nong Thale, Mueang Krabi, right on the Andaman Sea. It's about 20 minutes' drive from Ao Nang and roughly 30–40 minutes from Krabi Airport (KBV). Book the resort transfer or rent a car, as Grab is hard to find in this area.

faq.q: How much does Nakamanda Resort cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 6,000/night for a garden-view Sala Villa (around 56 sqm). Above that are sea-view Sala Villas and the Jacuzzi Villa Seaview with a private tub, up to a two-bedroom Pool Villa Seaview. Prices vary by date and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Nakamanda Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, honeymooners and anyone wanting a quiet beach villa. The mood is private and design-led with teak villas. It's less suited to travellers who want nightlife or to eat outside the resort every meal, since it's a fair way from Ao Nang and has plenty of steps for anyone with limited mobility.

faq.q: What is the beach in front of the resort like — can you swim?
faq.a: Klong Muang Beach here is a quiet, private stretch of sand looking out over the Andaman Sea and limestone karsts. You can swim at high tide (at low tide the water retreats quite far, as it does along the Klong Muang–Tubkaak coast). It's a much calmer spot than Ao Nang Beach.

faq.q: What are the restaurants like — is there much choice?
faq.a: There's the beachfront Naga Terrace, serving Thai and international dishes. Breakfast has a live cooking station for eggs and made-to-order drinks and is well liked. The honest caveat: the lunch/dinner menu isn't very varied and service can be slow, typical of a small resort far from town.

faq.q: How far ahead should you book, and is cancellation flexible?
faq.a: In high season (November–April), book 1–2 months ahead, especially for sea-view and Jacuzzi villas, which sell out fast given there are only 39 villas. Most platforms offer a Free Cancellation option — choose that if your plans aren't firm yet.
